A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neuron-explanation evaluation research despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original sampling and label-noise simulations, MTurk validation, automated explanation comparisons, and a crowdsourced study of two vision models.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulations and crowdsourced results, including additional component ablations, model comparisons, and annotator-agreement measurements.

M1.justification: The importance-sampling and Bayesian-aggregation pipeline is retained with procedural refinements. V2 replaces epsilon-based sampling regularization with an explicit 80% model-guided/20% uniform mixture and changes the stated activation normalization from sample to full-dataset statistics. Appendix B.4 also introduces an optional per-input/concept error-rate model, while retaining constant error rates for the main method.

E1.justification: The visual datasets, neuron-explanation tasks, and evaluated ResNet-50/ViT layers remain unchanged. V2 Appendix C.7 adds an author-annotator cohort for comparison with MTurk workers, providing limited additional population coverage.

E2.justification: The explanation-method sets in the automated and large-scale human comparisons are retained. However, the MTurk aggregation comparison adds SigLIP-only evaluation and no longer displays averaging alongside the other aggregators (v1 Figure 3b versus v2 Figure 11). V2 Table 4 also adds majority-vote aggregation to the large-scale study, previously reported only with Bayesian aggregation.

E3.justification: Validation changes from five selected neurons with 300 inputs each to ten randomly selected, non-vague neurons with 600 inputs each; nine raters per input are retained. The large study changes from 90 inputs with two raters to 180 with three. Simulated noise rises from 13% to 23%, beta changes from 0.01 to 0.05, and RCE changes from mean per-neuron relative error to summed absolute errors normalized by summed ground-truth correlations. V2 also adds full-dataset aggregation-only and author-rating controls.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit joint-versus-separate sampling/aggregation controls, mixture-weight sensitivity, heterogeneous error-model testing, automated-only evaluation comparisons, CLIP/SigLIP/SigLIP2 ablations, and author-versus-worker agreement analysis. Existing beta sensitivity and activation-only sampling analyses are revised, rather than wholly new. Appendix examples are also replaced and expanded to include ViT cases.

E5.justification: V1 reports standard errors and repeated sampling but no significance tests or agreement statistics. V2 adds two-sample Student's t-tests for explanation comparisons in Table 5 and Fleiss's kappa in Appendix C.7. Appendix B.2 newly specifies averaging its beta ablation over 30 random seeds; this does not establish an increase from v1's unspecified count for that analysis.

E6.justification: Automated Tables 1 and 2 retain their numerical results, but crowdsourced scores are extensively revised. For example, LE(SigLIP) with the SigLIP Bayesian prior changes from 0.2107 to 0.1803 on ResNet-50 and from 0.2382 to 0.2450 on ViT; the ResNet runner-up changes from CLIP-Dissect to INVERT. These are results under revised protocols, not same-setting gains or losses. V2 additionally reports substantial new ablation, significance, and agreement results.

T1.justification: The optimal-importance-sampling theorem and reproduced proof are retained, moving from B.3 to C.5. V2 explicitly states the proposal-support condition, revises the mathematical definition of RCE, corrects normalization expressions, and derives a posterior marginalizing per-input/concept error rates in B.4. These are substantive but bounded mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The central efficiency claim is substantially reduced: approximately 150-fold overall savings in v1 becomes approximately 40-fold in v2. Claimed sampling savings change from about 30-fold to 13–15-fold, and aggregation savings from about five-fold to three-fold. The contributions remain efficient full-distribution crowdsourced evaluation and comparison of explanation methods, with Linear Explanations still ranked best overall.

C2.justification: V2 develops budget-dependent applicability boundaries: automated-only evaluation for very small budgets, hybrid evaluation for intermediate budgets, and purely human evaluation for sufficiently large budgets (B.5). It also discusses ambiguous dataset labels, insufficient evidence for estimating individual error rates, and task ambiguity as a source of annotator disagreement. These substantially qualify practical interpretation, although the existing limitations in A.1 remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds OpenCLIP/model identifiers and specifies the alternative error model's fitted parameters and 100-bin integration approximation. The promised code repository destination changes, while hardware, runtime, worker eligibility, and payment details are retained. Reproducibility remains locally ambiguous: B.7 specifies SigLIP ViT-L-16-384 for sampling/aggregation, whereas C.3 retains the statement that all guidance uses SO400M.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Borowski et al.'s feature-visualization evaluation, OpenCLIP, and SigLIP2. Section 2.2 expands the distinction from activation-prediction/AUC-based human studies and clarifies the relationship to NeuronEval. The overall related-work coverage and positioning remain recognizable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are substantially rewritten, and MG-IS/BRAgg terminology is introduced throughout. Individual simulation studies are integrated into the method sections, Section 4 becomes combined validation, and the appendices are reorganized into discussion, ablations, and technical details with a new overview.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, Figure 1 is redrawn, and the principal human results gain a bar-chart presentation with detailed tables moved to the appendix. Numerous analysis plots and a significance table are added; example-neuron panels and their color thresholds are revised. The unchanged complex-explanation table is relocated rather than removed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central evaluation pipeline. Joint component controls, guiding-model and error-model ablations, automated-only comparisons, and annotator-agreement measurements address important gaps in v1's evidence about reliability and dependence on modeling choices. Significance tests also make the explanation-ranking evidence more assessable, including nonsignificant comparisons. Conflicting SigLIP specifications remain a reproducibility weakness, but the added validation and clearer applicability boundaries outweigh that limitation.
